items.title: Section: Five Qualities Before Embracing Someone, and Five Aptitudes for Where to Place Them

items.zh: 當知觀人二時差別。一、攝受時，二、處置時。於攝受時，應以五相觀察其人，然後攝受。一、由歸誠，二、由技能，三、由智慧，四、由行迹，五、由廉儉。於處置時，亦以五相觀察其人，然後處置。一、堪處事業，置事業中；二、堪處思業，置思業中；三、堪處和業，置和業中；四、堪處護身財業，置護身財業中；五、堪處法業，置法業中。
items.en: It should be understood that observing people differs across two moments — the moment of embracing them, and the moment of placing them. When embracing someone, five qualities should be observed: sincere devotion, skill, wisdom, conduct, and frugality. When placing someone, five aptitudes should likewise be observed: fitness for practical work, placed in practical affairs; fitness for deliberative work, placed where judgement is needed; fitness for harmonising work, placed in fostering harmony; fitness for protecting body and property, placed in that protective role; and fitness for the Dharma itself, placed in that pursuit.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Giving, Five Ways to Never Betray a Trust, and Five Fronts of Vigilance

items.zh: 捨略有五：一、田地捨，二、財物捨，三、隨宜捨，四、飲食捨，五、最勝捨。此中捨相、捨具名捨。賢善行者，為性於他無所違負，無所欺誑。無所違負，復有五種。一、無顛倒違負，二、無委信違負，三、無承事違負，四、無契約違負，五、無他方便違負。不放逸者，謂修習諸善法，防護不善心。因果相屬故，俱應為彼相。此復有五種應知。一、求財不放逸，二、守財不放逸，三、護身不放逸，四、護名不放逸，五、行法不放逸。
items.en: Giving is, in brief, of five kinds: giving land, giving wealth, giving what is appropriate, giving food, and the most excellent giving. Virtuous conduct is a disposition that neither betrays nor deceives others. Not betraying is of five further kinds: no deceptive betrayal, no betrayal of entrusted confidence, no betrayal of promised service, no betrayal of a contract, and no other scheme to betray. Non-negligence is the cultivation of wholesome qualities together with guarding against unwholesome mind. This is likewise of five kinds: non-negligence in seeking wealth, in guarding wealth, in protecting the body, in protecting one's name, and in practising the Dharma.

items.title: Section: Five Powers, Five Fortunes — Closing the Teaching on Auspiciousness

items.zh: 如是一切，總有五力能生吉祥。一、善尸羅力，二、善朋友力，三、無弊悋力，四、可委信力，五、法力。當知吉祥亦有五種。一、眾所愛樂，二、富貴自在，三、怨敵退伏，四、饒益所依，五、往諸善趣。前四種力，總能生起四種吉祥；第五一力，能生第五。問：幾根先煩惱業之所感得？答：八。
items.en: All of this together generates five powers producing auspiciousness: the power of good ethical discipline, the power of good companionship, the power of freedom from stinginess, the power of being genuinely relied upon, and the power of the Dharma. It should be understood that auspiciousness likewise has five kinds: being loved by all, wealth and freedom, enemies retreating in submission, benefiting one's own being, and proceeding to fortunate destinations. The first four powers together generate the first four fortunes; the fifth power alone generates the fifth. Question: how many faculties are obtained as a result of prior affliction and karma? Answer: eight.

items.title: Section: Which Faculties Need Guarding, Which Need Calming, and Which Are Already Composed

items.zh: 問：幾根名色為緣？答：一。問：幾根觸為緣？答：五。問：幾根策勵為緣？答：八。問：幾根應防護？答：八。問：幾根應調靜？答：一。問：幾根應寂止？答：五。問：幾根自性調順、寂靜、寂止，復能調伏、寂靜、寂止？答：八。
items.en: Question: how many faculties result from name-and-form as their condition? Answer: one. Question: from contact as their condition? Answer: five. Question: from sustained exertion as their condition? Answer: eight. Question: how many faculties should be protected? Answer: eight. Question: how many should be calmed? Answer: one. Question: how many should be stilled? Answer: five. Question: how many are, by their own nature, composed, still, and calm, and can also produce that same composure, stillness, and calm? Answer: eight.

items.title: Section: What Separates a Hearer's Faculties From a Bodhisattva's

items.zh: 云何諸根捨？謂同分界地諸根滅，餘生起。云何諸根棄？謂不同分界地諸根滅，餘生起。云何諸根斷？謂斷彼繫縛一切煩惱。云何諸根退？謂世間興盛若定、若生所有失壞。問：聲聞、獨覺、菩薩諸根，有何差別？答：當知差別略有五種。一、品類差別，二、任持差別，三、羂索差別，四、正行差別，五、證得差別。
items.en: What is relinquishing faculties? Faculties belonging to the same category of realm and stage cease, and others of that same category arise. What is discarding faculties? Faculties belonging to a different category of realm and stage cease, and others of that different category arise. What is severing faculties? Cutting off all the affliction that has bound them. What is regressing faculties? Worldly flourishing, whether meditative attainment or favourable rebirth, subsequently being lost. Question: what distinguishes the faculties of a hearer, a solitary realiser, and a bodhisattva? Answer: the distinction should be understood as, in brief, five kinds — a difference in category, in sustaining power, in what binds, in proper conduct, and in what is attained.

items.title: Section: Five Ways a Bodhisattva's Faculties Genuinely Differ from a Hearer's

items.zh: 品類差別者，諸菩薩根，其性上品；聲聞、獨覺所有諸根，軟品、中品。任持差別者，諸菩薩根，一切明處善巧任持；聲聞、獨覺所有諸根，一分明處善巧任持。羂索差別者，諸菩薩根，大悲所羂；聲聞、獨覺根不如是。正行差別者，諸菩薩根，自利利他正行現前；聲聞、獨覺所有諸根，自利現前。證得差別者，諸菩薩根，證得無上大菩提果；聲聞、獨覺所有諸根，證得下中二菩提果。
items.en: Concerning category: a bodhisattva's faculties are, by nature, of the highest grade; a hearer's and solitary realiser's faculties are of the mild and middling grades. Concerning sustaining power: a bodhisattva's faculties skilfully sustain every field of knowledge; a hearer's and solitary realiser's sustain only a portion. Concerning what binds them: a bodhisattva's faculties are bound by great compassion; a hearer's and solitary realiser's faculties are not. Concerning proper conduct: a bodhisattva's faculties manifest both self-benefit and benefiting others; a hearer's and solitary realiser's manifest only self-benefit. Concerning attainment: a bodhisattva's faculties attain the unsurpassed fruit of great awakening; a hearer's and solitary realiser's attain the lesser and middling fruits of awakening.

items.title: Section: Sharp Faculties, Dull Faculties, and Whether Joy Arises the Moment One Attains the Fruit

items.zh: 問：若補特伽羅依未至定修諦現觀，彼得果時，起初靜慮喜根現前，為不起耶？答：有一能起，有一不起。若有利根，眾多善本之所資助，彼能現起，非餘。
items.en: Question: for one relying on access concentration to directly realise the truths, does the joy of the first absorption arise at the moment of attaining the fruit, or not? Answer: some can give rise to it, others cannot. Whoever has sharp faculties, supported by an abundance of wholesome roots, can give rise to it — no one else can.

items.title: Section: Which Faculties Can Actually Enter Each Absorption, and Why Bodhisattvas Avoid the Formless Attainments

items.zh: 問：幾根入初靜慮？答：八。後三，一分能入，一分不能。如初靜慮，第二亦爾。第三亦八。然非即彼。第四靜慮及無色定，七根能入。後三，有一能入，有一不能。
items.en: Question: how many faculties enter the first absorption? Answer: eight. Of the final three, one portion can enter, one cannot. As with the first absorption, so too the second. The third is likewise, yet not quite the same eight. The fourth absorption and the formless attainments admit seven faculties. Of the final three, one kind of practitioner can enter, another cannot.

items.title: Section: Counting the Faculties Behind Each of the Four Fruits

items.zh: 問：幾根得預流果？答：或一、或八。或二、或九得一來果。憂根雖道所依，非道攝故，此中不取。喜根非堅住故，此亦不取。若通取者，當增其數。問：幾根得不還果？答：或十一、或二。憂根道理，如前應知。問：幾根得阿羅漢果？答：或一、或十。
items.en: Question: how many faculties attain the fruit of stream-entry? Answer: either one, or eight. Either two, or nine attain the fruit of once-returning. Question: how many attain the fruit of non-returning? Answer: either eleven, or two — the sorrow faculty's own status explained as before. Question: how many attain the fruit of arhatship? Answer: either one, or ten.

blocks.text: The teaching on an auspicious life ends, and the treatise compares the faculties of hearers and bodhisattvas.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a person is placed among those of their kind; the ability to carry out tasks is practical work, and weighing matters is deliberation.
Non-negligence is cultivating the wholesome and guarding against the unwholesome. Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, discipline and restraint of the senses.
The first four powers together generate four fortunes, the fifth alone the fifth. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of discipline comes through patience and gentleness.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical faculties and life must be guarded from grasping outer objects. The mind should be tamed and quiet, undisturbed by pain, pleasure, sorrow, joy, or equanimity.
Bodhisattvas are of the highest grade, hearers mild, solitary realisers middling.
Master Cháng Bǎi: caught in beings' birth and death, a bodhisattva vows through countless eons to save beings there; this is a bodhisattva's nature.
Master Cháng Bǎi: sharp practitioners can raise the joy of the first absorption; dull ones cannot.
Placing people where they fit is part of the path, too.

quiz.q: What are the two moments of observing people, and the five placements?
options: giving and keeping precepts; devotion, skill, wisdom, conduct, frugality
ordination and lay life; the five precepts
embracing and placing; practical, deliberative, harmonising, protective, and Dharma work
birth and death; the five aggregates
quiz.why: The treatise gives embracing and placing. Master Cháng Bǎi: at placing, a person is put among those of their kind; ability to carry out tasks is practical work, and weighing matters is deliberative work. Devotion, skill, wisdom, conduct, and frugality are the five observed at embracing. A striking administrative teaching for the laity.

quiz.q: What is non-negligence, and what are its five kinds?
options: no drinking or gambling; the five non-betrayals
cultivating the wholesome and guarding against the unwholesome; in seeking and guarding wealth, body, name, and Dharma
constant absorption; the five givings
reciting the Buddha's name; the five powers
quiz.why: The treatise defines non-negligence as cultivating the wholesome and guarding against the unwholesome. Master Cháng Bǎi gives discipline and restraint of the faculties as examples. The five include worldly affairs, seeking and guarding wealth, as the teaching is for those still enjoying sense pleasure. The five non-betrayals belong to virtuous conduct.

quiz.q: How do the five powers and five fortunes correspond?
options: the Dharma power generates all five; ethical discipline generates fortunate destinations
the first four generate the first four; the Dharma power generates fortunate destinations
all five generate one fortune
all fortunes come from friends
quiz.why: The treatise says the first four powers together generate four fortunes and the fifth alone the fifth. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of discipline comes through patience and gentleness; freedom from stinginess is giving. So the five powers gather the five conditions of §57. The English "fortunes" and "auspiciousness" render one Chinese word.

quiz.q: How do relinquishing, discarding, severing, and regressing differ?
options: relinquishing: different realm; discarding: same realm; severing: the faculties ending; regressing: losing the noble path
all four are synonyms
relinquishing wholesome, discarding evil, severing life, regressing physical
relinquishing: same realm; discarding: different realm; severing: cutting bonds; regressing: losing worldly flourishing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for relinquishing, a desire-realm being dies, its faculties cease, and those of another ripened body arise in the same realm; discarding is leaving one realm's faculties for those of a different one. Severing concerns the bonds, not the faculties themselves, as the treatise says.

quiz.q: Which eight should be protected, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: faith and the rest with the three, gained by practice and easily lost, and so to be guarded
the feelings and the three
mind and the seven physical
the seven physical faculties and life, not letting them grasp outer objects
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seven physical faculties and the life faculty are these eight; they must be guarded so as not to grasp outer objects. Faith and the rest with the three are the eight that come from exertion, in the prior question. The English "protected" is apt.

quiz.q: What are the five differences among the faculties of the three vehicles?
options: category, sustaining power, what binds, proper conduct, attainment
faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, the three differing in strength
the three realms, vision, cultivation
giving, ethics, patience, diligence, absorption
quiz.why: The treatise lists category, sustaining power, what binds, proper conduct, and attainment. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas are of the highest grade, hearers mild, and solitary realisers middling; a hearer's arhatship is the lesser fruit of awakening and a solitary realiser's the middling one.

quiz.q: The English has "bound by great compassion" and "what binds" for 羂索. Why does this work, and how does the lecture explain it?
options: it keeps the sense of being bound: compassion snares the bodhisattva in saṃsāra, vowing to save beings for countless eons
poor: 羂索 is another name for affliction, so it should be "freed by", bodhisattvas having left saṃsāra
poor: it should be "decorated by"
poor: the Chinese says hearers are bound
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: snared within beings' birth and death, a bodhisattva vows through countless eons to save beings there; this is a bodhisattva's nature. The English "bound by great compassion" keeps the striking image of a snare, turning what would be a fault into a virtue.

quiz.q: Which should be calmed, which stilled, and why?
options: calm the mind, leaving affliction; still the five feelings, free of their disturbance, so the mind stays quiet and makes no karma
calm life to lengthen it; still the five physical faculties, the mind then being quiet
calm faith; still the five wholesome ones
calm the tongue; still the three
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind faculty should be tamed so as to leave afflictions and be quiet; without the disturbance of pain, pleasure, sorrow, joy, and equanimity, mind stays calm and still and makes no karma through unstable moods. The English "calmed" and "stilled" render 調靜 and 寂止.

quiz.q: Can one relying on access concentration raise the first absorption's joy at attaining the fruit?
options: all can, joy being certain at the fruit, regardless of sharpness
none can, access concentration having no joy
only arhats can
those of sharp faculties supported by wholesome roots can; dull ones cannot
quiz.why: The treatise says some can and some cannot. Master Cháng Bǎi: sharp practitioners can raise the joy of the first absorption; dull ones cannot. He adds that only access concentration before the first absorption can directly reach the fruit. The English "access concentration" is a good term for 未至定.
